content_metadata.description: This video features former Love Island participants discussing the challenges and emotional impacts of experiencing break-ups while in the public eye. The narrative is presented as personal anecdotes and reflections, aiming to inform viewers about the complexities of handling public relationships on a reality TV platform.

It was about two weeks I didn't leave my house I was just thinking to myself 'what you're gonna do Marce? Your friends and your mom and your dad and close family members Whereas I walk down the street now and people go 'Why are you still not with Kaz?' I'm like 'Geezer, just let me be!' Negative people will obviously always bring you down but that's why it's always good to speak to the people who won't be negative towards you to speak to the people that have positive energy for you so your friends your family like those are the people you need to speak to. You don't need to go on social media and be worrying about what other people are saying to you I remember like thinking 'Wow we're gonna have to break up' and then thinking Instead of your first words being 'How do I feel?' It was like 'What's everyone gonna say?' Like 'What's the press coverage gonna be?' like 'What my boys gonna say?' what are all those people that you know when they said like how's it going and you're telling them 'yeah it's fine, it's good' and then a week later you're like No, we're not together anymore It can be an amazing thing to know that people support you but also the hardest thing for me was never being able to avoid that person everywhere I turned everyone was messaging me things all of the time... if my ex-boyfriend would go to a bar and I'd have five girls messaging me and say and tell me what he was up to and document what he was doing for someone who's trying to process the end of a relationship get over it and move on having that still kind of feeding into your life when you don't necessarily want it is something that I don't think I'd necessarily have to go through if I wasn't in the public eye and my relationship wasn't formed in the way it was I get really low lows and really high highs and I was publicly cheated on and that made me mad I think traumatic experiences like heartbreak and like moving away and stuff really stressed me out so that's when the anxiety happens and then anxiety I get all the time because I overthink all the time I mean I'm just being human i sat in my room for like two whole days just being like 'what the (bleep) is gonna happen' Wes called me and just went 'You'll be fine' because I was just sat there in my own head kind of creating scenarios that just weren't gonna happen or that weren't likely to happen so it took someone who'd been through it just to say like 'yo you're gonna be fine'

youtube_description:
It's no secret that many of Love Island's former couples don't go the distance. Aside from the lucky few, most former Islanders will split - often within months of the series ending.

This week, 2019's Anton Danyluk and Belle Hassan called time on their relationship, and now Amber Gill and Greg O’Shea have split up too, just five short weeks since winning this year’s series of the ITV2 reality show.

Here, former Love Islanders explain what it's REALLY like to go through a break-up in the public eye.

Featuring:
Marcel Somerville, series 3 (2017)
Samira Mighty, series 4 (2018)
Charlie Brake, series 4 (2018)
Josh Denzel, series 4 (2018)
Zara McDermott, series 4 (2018)
